detail.abstract: This study examines the key determinants of Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections across 17 Indian States from 2019 to 2025. The States are categorised into two clusters based on development indicators such as per capita income, infrastructure quality, and the degree of informality in their economies. The results indicate that both per capita income and financial development have a positive and significant impact on GST revenues, underscoring the scope for enhancing tax collection by raising income levels and strengthening credit absorption through financial development.

title: Mind the Concession: Headline Rents versus Effective Rents
affiliations: UCL - University College London and University of St. Gallen - School of Finance

detail.title: Mind the Concession: Headline Rents versus Effective Rents

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no funding.

detail.abstract: The price written into a contract need not be the price that matters economically. We study this distinction using commercial leases in London, United Kingdom, for which both headline rent-the visible price used in comparables, valuations, and market reporting-and effective rent net of concessions are observable. We first show that unusually high headline rents are systematically bundled with larger concessions. Following new rail station openings, nearby leases exhibit narrower concession wedges than comparison leases, confirming that concessions operate as genuine price-adjustment margins. Our central test exploits the transition from old UK GAAP to FRS 102, which reduced the usefulness of rent-free concessions as a contractpackaging device. In more exposed market segments, contracts shift toward fewer rent-free months and narrower concession wedges, while effective rents show no robust differential change. Institutional rules can therefore reshape the price markets observe without materially changing the bargain underneath.

title: Actionwise Maximin Equilibrium

detail.title: Actionwise Maximin Equilibrium

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare that I have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant.

detail.abstract: In this note, we define an equilibrium concept called actionwise maximin equilibrium (AME). A set strategy is simply a nonempty set of possible actions. An AME evaluates such a set strategy profile through its lower payoff envelope, pointwise over the opponents' possible actions. A unilateral deviation is profitable only if it yields a payoff strictly above the lower envelope at every opponent action. We show that a set strategy profile is an AME if no pure action strictly improves on this lower envelope at every opponents' action profile contained in the opponents' set strategies. Pure Nash equilibria are exactly the singleton AMEs.

title: Strict Pre-Onset Prediction of Atrial Fibrillation from Long-Term ECG with Evaluation of Dataset Expansion and Cross-Database Generalization

detail.title: Strict Pre-Onset Prediction of Atrial Fibrillation from Long-Term ECG with Evaluation of Dataset Expansion and Cross-Database Generalization
detail.abstract: Short-term forecasting of atrial fibrillation (AF) onset could support proactive monitoring, but reported performance depends strongly on the temporal definition and validation design. Long-term ECG recordings from LTAF, AFDB, and SHDB-AF were analysed using a 10-min input window ending 10 min before AF onset. AF episodes lasting at least 30 s were retained, intervals separated by 30 s or less were merged, and the final extraction required at least 20 min of AF-free pre-onset data. Group-wise five-fold cross-validation prevented recordings or repeated subject-level records from crossing evaluation groups. RR-based models were compared with a 1,073,857-parameter scale-matched raw-ECG CNN. The final cohort contained 203 matched positive-negative pairs (406 windows), comprising 69 LTAF, 26 AFDB, and 108 SHDB-AF pairs. Pooled out-of-fold AUROC was 0.585 for RR, 0.583 for RR plus PAF-derived information, and 0.534 for the raw-ECG CNN (95% CI 0.495–0.574). In leave-one-database-out evaluation, RR-plus-PAF AUROC was 0.590, 0.526, and 0.569 for LTAF, AFDB, and SHDB-AF, respectively, whereas the corresponding database-stratified pooled out-of-fold AUROCs for the raw CNN were 0.546, 0.538, and 0.524. In a common 155-pair horizon analysis, AUROC was numerically highest at 10 min (0.597), although the difference between the 10-min and 5-min horizons was small (0.0093, 95% CI -0.020 to 0.039). These findings indicate that strict pre-onset AF forecasting contains modest and database-dependent predictive information, with RR dynamics being at least as informative as the substantially more complex raw-waveform benchmark.

title: Communication and Cooperation with Human and Artificial Agents
affiliations: Stony Brook University, Brown University and Stony Brook University

detail.title: Communication and Cooperation with Human and Artificial Agents

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to Declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: Approved by Stony Brook University #IRB2023-00402.
declarations.funderStatement: Funded provided by Stony Brook University

detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Large Language Models (LLMs) in
particular, have recently been the subjects of keen focus. These
models are advancing at a rapid pace, nearing human-level com-
petence in generating language. It seems inevitable that they will
begin, and continue, to play significant roles in our daily lives, me-
diating interactions with other humans in social, economic, and
cultural realms. Here we investigate the effect of LLMs in social
dilemmas (defined by the tension between individual and collective
rationality) [21]. Studies have consistently found that allowing com-
munication among participants in social dilemmas increases the
number of people working for the mutual benefit of the group [3].
In this study, we explore how the presence of LLMs affects coopera-
tion in standard one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma and Stag Hunt games.
We compare experimental conditions featuring algorithmic agents
with and without communication to control conditions featuring
human-to-human interactions, again both with and without com-
munication. The presence of communication significantly increased
prosocial behavior, but the agent type of the other player did not
have a significant effect.

title: An Analysis of the Global Networks of Portfolio Investment
affiliations: European Systemic Risk Board

detail.title: An Analysis of the Global Networks of Portfolio Investment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no competing interests to declare that are relevant to the content of this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for conducting this paper.

detail.abstract: Combining data of EU countries from the international investment position, as reported to Eurostat, with the IMF Portfolio Investment Positions by Counterpart Economy, I build a dataset of portfolio investments in equity and investment fund shares, and in debt securities comprising 51 countries and jurisdictions. Setting 2024 as reference date, the two related networks identify the United States and offshore financial centres as key nodes. Network metrics are used to identify countries at the core of the networks, more affected by shocks and belonging to communities. Advanced economies still dominate both global networks, suggesting that their financial systems are developed enough to channel domestic savings into global financial assets. A comparison with 2014 reveals a large increase in portfolio equity and investment fund shares, even after accounting for inflation, changes in exchange rates and changes in stock prices. The increase is particularly acute for United States and jurisdictions associated with investment funds (i.e., Luxembourg, Ireland and offshore financial centres). Regarding the network of debt securities, there is a large increase in in debt securities issued in the United States since 2014, while investment of the United States abroad increases modestly. Changes in foreign portfolio investment of most European countries is small or even negative, probably signalling the effects of the sovereign debt crisis on the attractiveness of their debt securities. The methodology used to build these networks can be easily replicated and can provide useful information to macroprudential authorities in the assessment of vulnerabilities in the global financial system.

title: Joint Identification of Information Generation and Uptake in Protocol-Coupled Belief Dynamics

detail.title: Joint Identification of Information Generation and Uptake in Protocol-Coupled Belief Dynamics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is theoretical and does not involve human participants, patients, personal data, or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Belief dynamics depend jointly on how information is generated and how a receiver incorporates it. We study the inverse problem of separating these two mechanisms from a belief trajectory. For a finite-state model in natural log-odds coordinates, the update is η t+1 = η t + Aℓ et,mt (d), where d governs the observation protocol and A is an unknown uptake transformation. Conditional on a realized observation path, scalar uptake A = λI implies Z = λE ω (d), so only the positivescale class of protocol-generated evidence is identified. We derive exact and regular first-order conditions for separating protocol from uptake and show that repeated proportional evidence is insufficient. If E ω (d) = H ω (Ψ(d)), dimensions collapsed by Ψ remain unidentified from conditional belief dynamics, yielding a distinct mechanism-protocol confounding layer. For operator-valued uptake A in a matrix Lie group, protocol identification is governed by evidence orbits and uptake identification by stabilizers. A pullback Fisher-Rao metric quantifies weak separation after projecting out uptake-generated trajectory directions. Finite-state examples illustrate the theory. In the three-prisoners special case, unknown positive uptake destroys generic single-posterior identification of the disclosure probability, while the equal-prior half posterior still identifies the boundary q = 1; under the earlier coupling this identifies d = (0, 0, 1), but not λ.

title: Frequency-Timing Constraints on the Origin of Antigen-Negative Relapse in CD19 CAR-T Therapy: A Minimal ODE Model
affiliations: Osaka University and  Independent Researcher

detail.title: Frequency-Timing Constraints on the Origin of Antigen-Negative Relapse in CD19 CAR-T Therapy: A Minimal ODE Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: Antigen-negative relapse limits the durability of CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T therapy in Bcell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (B-ALL). We build a minimal four-state ordinary differential equation (ODE) model coupling effector and memory CART populations to antigen-positive and antigen-negative tumour compartments, with antigen escape represented as a mutational flux. CART kinetics are calibrated to published biexponential persistence data; the antigen-escape process is anchored to the clinically observed early timing of high-burden CD19-negative relapse. Rather than fitting a single escape parameter set, we treat the escape rate and escape-clone growth rate as a solution family to expose their non-identifiability. Using a virtual population, we ask whether a single, uniform, deterministic escape flux can jointly reproduce the observed frequency and timing of antigen-negative relapse. It cannot: reproducing early relapse forces the antigen-negative relapse frequency far above the clinically observed rate. The constraint identifies a limitation of uniform deterministic escape without uniquely determining the underlying population structure, motivating explicitly heterogeneous or stochastic formulations.

title: The Same Afternoon: A Forensic Case Study Testing the United Nations Finding that Venezuela's Repressive Apparatus Remains Intact

detail.title: The Same Afternoon: A Forensic Case Study Testing the United Nations Finding that Venezuela's Repressive Apparatus Remains Intact

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author discloses no financial relationship with any person or organization that could be perceived to have influenced this study. For transparency, the author discloses a non-financial professional history relevant to the subject matter: he is a former Venezuelan public prosecutor and a source certified by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) for its 2018-2019 report on Venezuela, and he is the founder of a security consultancy (LISE) that publishes commentary on Venezuelan organized crime and human rights matters. This history is disclosed and discussed at length in Section II of the paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper does not involve human-subjects research requiring ethics board approval. It consists of a documentary and forensic analysis of a single audiovisual file that had already been published and circulated publicly on social media in connection with a matter of significant public interest and public record (the September 17, 2026 apprehension of a public political figure, reported contemporaneously by multiple independent news outlets). No interviews, surveys, experiments, or private data collection involving human participants were conducted by the author. No non-public or personally identifying information beyond what was already publicly reported was used.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author through the Latino Institute for Security Efficiency (LISE), without grant support, sponsorship, or financial contribution from any government, organization, or third party.

detail.abstract: This working paper examines whether the institutional continuity documented by the United Nations Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela in its September 16, 2026 report, describing a repressive apparatus that "remains intact" eight months after the capture of Nicolas Maduro, can be observed at the level of an individual case rather than only in aggregate. On September 17, 2026, the day Venezuela's government and opposition opened the second cycle of their political dialogue, security personnel detained Javier Oropeza, former mayor of the Torres municipality (Carora, Lara state), hours after a press interview and less than forty-eight hours after his return from two years of exile. This paper presents an original forensic audiovisual analysis of the publicly circulated video of that apprehension, conducted under a documented chain-of-custody and file-integrity protocol, and situates its findings against the Mission's own conclusions, including its identification of at least nineteen officials previously named for grave human rights violations who continue to occupy key positions in the current government. The author writes from a dual vantage point: as a former Venezuelan public prosecutor, and as a source certified by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) for its 2018-2019 comprehensive report on the human rights situation in Venezuela, a report that first documented several of the same institutional patterns the Mission describes as unresolved eight years later. The paper does not conclude that the Oropeza apprehension was unlawful; consistent with the underlying forensic report's own limitations, several material facts cannot be established from the available video. Its contribution is methodological and comparative: it offers a replicable protocol for documenting contested state-security incidents close to real time, and it shows that a single, contemporaneously documented case can be read productively alongside a systemic UN finding published one day earlier, without either source substituting for the other.

title: Linked Characteristics Are Covariances: The Asset-Pricing Content of Economic Linkages

detail.title: Linked Characteristics Are Covariances: The Asset-Pricing Content of Economic Linkages

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have nothing to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: I have nothing to declare.

detail.abstract: Firms interact with each other. They buy from suppliers, sell to customers, and share an industry or a product market; those economically linked firms have comoving fundamentals. However, modern characteristics-based factor-model literature conditions on a firm's own characteristics, leaving asset-pricing implications of linked-firm information understudied. This paper asks whether characteristics of linked firms carry systematic, priced information beyond the firm's own, and if so, how. Averaging peer characteristics over eleven networks and adding them to a 35-characteristic conditional factor model estimated strictly out of sample from 1973 to 2022, I document a significant annualized tangency-portfolio Sharpe ratio rise from 3.16 to 4.07. Further, the linked-firm information (i) partially subsumes the lead-lag momentum in the literature; (ii) forecasts future fundamentals and fundamental comovements; (iii) delivers additional asset-pricing power mainly through a covariance channel, while an information-diffusion explanation cannot account for the evidence. Finally, I provide a fourtype classification of the individual linkage set based on each linkage's fundamental content and contribution to the priced span. Overall, the evidence is consistent with linked characteristics acting as conditioning information about a firm's place in a comovement structure, and it provides a factor-exposure-based interpretation of the lead-lag predictability literature.

title: What a Legal Knowledge Graph cannot Check about Itself: A Source Audit of a Deployed EU Medical-AI Ontology

detail.title: What a Legal Knowledge Graph cannot Check about Itself: A Source Audit of a Deployed EU Medical-AI Ontology

The author developed MAILO, the ontology audited in this study; this self-audit relationship is disclosed in the manuscript as a potential source of authorial bias.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants, patients, or interventions. It is a source audit of a legal knowledge graph based on publicly available legal materials and repository artefacts.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
Logical consistency and constraint conformance show whether a legal knowledge graph satisfies its encoded model; they do not show whether the encoded assertions correspond to the legal sources they cite. 

This paper reports a source audit of MAILO, a deployed OWL 2 and SHACL ontology of EU medical-AI regulatory obligations. The source-audit programme analysed here culminated in MAILO v5.2.0 (1,859 triples); the current repository release is v5.2.3 (1,946 triples). Across the historical audit programme, all nine paragraph citations encoding the CJEU automated-decision trilogy required correction, all ten encoded cross-framework tension instances required correction or model harmonisation, and two encoded legal propositions had their normative character inverted. The item-level worksheet maintained for this study records 53 correction entries in the dataset culminating in v5.2.0; later releases are analytically separate and are not retroactively counted as part of it. Legal difficulty is not operationalised and no statistical association with detectability is estimated. Instead, within the paper's internal-detectability definition, corrections classed as detectable coincided with a second, independently constraining representation of the relevant fact. Adding explicit InclusionBasis and EncodingBasis declarations made additional provenance and scope checks expressible. I argue that representation supplies a necessary condition for internally detecting source mismatches, while residual legal review remains necessary where no disagreement-capable representation exists.

title: Cuba's Incomplete Marketization: Institutional Reform in a State-dominated Hybrid Economy
affiliations: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) and Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) - NTNU Business School

detail.title: Cuba's Incomplete Marketization: Institutional Reform in a State-dominated Hybrid Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Public funded

detail.abstract: Recent economic reforms have expanded the role of private enterprise, non-state employment, foreign investment, and market-based exchange in Cuba. However, these reforms have not displaced the state's dominant role in strategic sectors, capital allocation, foreign exchange, and the institutional regulation of non-state activity. Drawing on policy documents, legislation, interview material from 2013, observations, and scholarly and contemporary sources, this article evaluates Cuba's economic system across six institutional dimensions: international economic cooperation, capital and investment policy, ownership, production decisions, employment, and welfare. We argue that Cuba has moved away from classical comprehensive central planning but has not developed a socialist market economy comparable to China or Vietnam. The Cuban economy is better characterized as a state-dominated hybrid or partial-reform socialist economy undergoing incomplete marketization. The reform program introduced in 2026 could strengthen the role of private and foreign capital, but its longer-term significance will depend on implementation, institutional credibility, access to finance and foreign exchange, and the durability of the rules governing both state and non-state economic actors.

title: DGRNet: A Lightweight Dual-Graph Residual Network with Graph-Consistency Test-Time Adaptation for Motor Imagery EEG Classification
affiliations: Nanning Normal University, Nanning Normal University, Guangxi Academy of Sciences, Guangxi Academy of Sciences, Guangxi Academy of Sciences, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: DGRNet: A Lightweight Dual-Graph Residual Network with Graph-Consistency Test-Time Adaptation for Motor Imagery EEG Classification
detail.abstract: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) decode scalp EEG activity generated during imagined limb movement, providing an important route for non-invasive human-computer interaction, assistive control, and neurorehabilitation. However, motor imagery electroencephalography (MI-EEG) signals have low signal-to-noise ratios, strong non-stationarity, and substantial subject variability, requiring classification models to capture temporal patterns, channel relationships, and cross-session distribution changes under limited calibration samples and low deployment cost. Existing lightweight CNNs, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs), and attention-based decoders often absorb channel relationships implicitly through spatial convolution or attention weights, making it difficult to jointly exploit electrode topology, subject-specific functional dependence, and target-domain prediction stability. This paper proposes DGRNet, a lightweight dual-graph residual network for MI-EEG classification, which inserts a dual-graph residual propagation module before an attention-TCN decoder and injects a structural graph together with a training-derived functional graph into temporal convolutional features through residual channel propagation. We further propose Graph-Consistency Guided Test-Time Adaptation (GC-TTA), which stabilizes unlabeled target-sample inference by constraining prediction consistency among the dual-graph mixed view, structural-graph view, and functional-graph view. On BCIC-IV-2a, DGRNet achieves 86.15% accuracy, 0.8153 Kappa, and 86.09% Macro-F1; on BCIC-IV-2b and HGD, it achieves 80.85% and 93.35% accuracy, respectively. These results indicate that DGRNet combines explicit channel-relation modeling and inference-time stability constraints with low parameter overhead, providing a lightweight MI-EEG decoding framework that balances structural priors, subject variability, and test-time robustness.

title: WaveGate-nnU-Net: Frequency-Domain Inclusion Preserves Segmentation Accuracy under Reduced Training Data in Nasal and Paranasal Sinus CT
affiliations: Chang Gung University and Chang Gung University

detail.title: WaveGate-nnU-Net: Frequency-Domain Inclusion Preserves Segmentation Accuracy under Reduced Training Data in Nasal and Paranasal Sinus CT
detail.abstract: Background and Objectives: Automatic segmentation of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses from CT aids diagnosis and surgical planning, but clinical datasets in this domain remain small, which can affect training stability and evaluation validity. This study investigates whether frequency-domain representation learning can be incorporated, in a lightweight form, into the self-configuring nnU-Net framework, and whether the resulting performance improvement survives rigorous statistical validation.Methods: We constructed an nnU-Net with frequency inclusion, adding a multi-scale wavelet branch and a cross-domain attention module at the network bottleneck following a previously reported frequency-spatial dual-stream formulation, and corrected a zero-initialization gating deadlock in that formulation, using the corrected model (v2) as a common base. On this base, we evaluated three variants: X1, an input-conditioned learnable spectral gate applied to 24 wavelet sub-bands; X2, which adds a boundary-distance training objective; and WaveGate-nnU-Net (hereafter WaveGate), the proposed model combining both. Experiments used the 130-volume NasalSeg CT dataset, under a full 91/19/20 protocol and a 3-fold cross-validation in which the training set for each fold was reduced by approximately 19%, from 91 to 73-74 cases.Results: Under the full protocol, all variants showed a small but statistically detectable improvement over a matched nnU-Net baseline. WaveGate achieved a Dice score of 95.78% versus 95.59% for the baseline, an improvement of 0.19 percentage points (95% CI [0.09, 0.29]; Holm-adjusted p = 0.004), and WaveGate also reduced average surface distance (ASD) from 0.252 mm to 0.235 mm. WaveGate was statistically equivalent to either individual component within a margin of ±0.10 percentage points, suggesting a shared performance ceiling rather than a complementary gain. Under reduced training data, baseline Dice dropped by 2.71 percentage points (95.59% to 92.88%), while WaveGate remained essentially unchanged (95.78% to 95.75%), a cross-fold advantage of +2.88 percentage points (fold-level 95% CI [0.80, 4.96]) that held across all 20 test cases (sign test, p = 1.9×10⁻⁶) and was corroborated by average surface distance.Conclusions: The practical value of this combined approach lies primarily in within-distribution data efficiency, rather than in maximizing peak segmentation accuracy.

title: How Do Investment Behaviors Transmit Across Generations? The Effects of Parents and Neighborhoods
affiliations: and

detail.title: How Do Investment Behaviors Transmit Across Generations? The Effects of Parents and Neighborhoods

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no personal or financial relationship with any people or organizations involved in the study.
declarations.funderStatement: Clara Egehoved Tørsløv acknowledges financial support from the Center for Big Data in Finance (grant no. DNRF167).

detail.abstract: Financial outcomes are known to be highly persistent across generations. However, less is known about the exact process through which specific investment behaviors develop based on features of one's childhood. Using Danish administrative data and two quasi-experimental designs, we find a significant effect of childhood exposure to the behaviors of one's own parents, and of the parents of one's peers, on a child's investment behaviors in adulthood. We perform tests to shed light on the underlying structure of the "production function" of investment behaviors and find evidence of substitutability of exposure to own-parents and peer-parents. In exploring mechanisms, we find that direct transfers of public equity and the sharing of financial intermediaries cannot fully explain the parent-child transmission, suggesting that other channels, such as risk preferences or financial savvy, play a role.

title: Inference-Based Performance Evaluation Using the Sortino Ratio
affiliations: University of Zurich - Department of Economics and University of Zurich - Department of Economics

detail.title: Inference-Based Performance Evaluation Using the Sortino Ratio

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: The Sharpe ratio remains the most widely used measure of risk-adjusted performance, but in many practical settings the Sortino ratio is more appropriate because it focuses exclusively on downside risk-the type of risk investors care about most. For industry practitioners and applied researchers who rely on the Sortino ratio, we develop statistical methods for three fundamental inference problems: inference for the difference between two Sortino ratios; inference for a single Sortino ratio, and multiple testing based on Sortino ratios. Although sample estimates often suggest meaningful differences in performance, valid conclusions about population quantities require appropriate statistical inference. Our proposed methods accommodate key empirical features of financial returns, including non-normality, skewness, heavy tails, and serial dependence. We illustrate their practical relevance through several empirical applications based on real financial data.

title: Reframing "Habits" As Distinct "Economic Goods": A Novel "Individual Habit-Based Consumer Theory"

detail.title: Reframing "Habits" As Distinct "Economic Goods": A Novel "Individual Habit-Based Consumer Theory"

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This manuscript presents a purely theoretical microeconomic optimization framework and did not involve any human patients, participants, clinical trials, or animal testing.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was co-funded by the European Commission under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) COFUND programme (Grant Agreement No. 101081609, DIGI PLUS, HORIZON-MSCA-2021-COFUND-01) as part of the DIGI+ program.

detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper establishes a novel theoretical framework (Individual Habit-Based Consumer Theory) to reframe automatic habits as distinct economic goods, formalizing habit loop mechanics within rational choice theory to explain persistent, seemingly irrational human behaviors. Design/methodology/approach: The study develops an axiomatic microeconomic optimization model. Habits are treated as endogenous goods with non monetary prices derived from automaticity, inconsistency, and cue frequency, optimized under a constrained behavioral resource budget. Findings: Cumulative repetition endogenously lowers a habit’s behavioral price, creating a lock-in effect. This frames the intention-behavior gap as an economic optimization under high initial switching costs rather than psychological failure. Research limitations/implications: As a pure theoretical framework, this research lacks empirical validation. Future paradigms must experimentally test the proposed hypotheses using neuroimaging or automated behavioral tracking data collected via wearable technologies. Practical implications: Motivational interventions are inefficient if a behavior's initial resource barrier is too high. Practitioners should prioritize environmental choice architecture that systematically lowers the dynamic price of desirable habits through task simplification. Social implications: Policymakers can leverage this framework to scale public health and environmental campaigns. Shifting from information dissemination to structural cue design optimizes population welfare under limited cognitive or temporal resource constraints. Originality/value: This paper is the first to mathematically formalize the psychological habit loop within individual consumer theory. It uniquely redefines behavioral inertia as a structural problem of resource allocation under dynamic pricing.

title: Custodialism: How Machine Abundance Ends the Age of Human Necessity

detail.title: Custodialism: How Machine Abundance Ends the Age of Human Necessity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract: For the whole of human history, economic and political institutions have rested on a single condition: human effort was scarce, and therefore valuable, and therefore a source of leverage for those who supplied it. This paper argues that autonomous production, in which machines increasingly build and direct the machines, loosens the economy's dependence on human effort and, with it, that leverage. The argument does not require that machines surpass human capability everywhere or that all work disappear. It requires only that broad human economic necessity weaken across enough of the economy to erode the bargaining power on which meritocracy, markets, property, and rights were built. The result is a distinct order, here termed custodialism, in which people are provided for but no longer needed. Drawing on the task-based labor economics of Acemoglu and Restrepo and the distributional analysis of Korinek and Stiglitz, the paper frames this not as an inevitability but as a path that present choices can still redirect.

title: Emotional Regret Expected Value and the Resolution of the Allais Paradox: An EAV-EAEU Approach within Relative Rationality Theory

detail.abstract: This paper develops a Relative Rationality Theory resolution of the Allais Paradox through Emotional Regret Expected Value. The central argument is that, in the standard monetary representation of the Allais problem within Expected Utility Theory, identical monetary outcomes are represented by the same utility values across the two choice problems. In the classical Allais structure, this contextinvariant representation permits the common-consequence cancellation that generates the contradiction between the observed preferences 𝐴 1 ≻ 𝐵 1 and 𝐵 2 ≻ 𝐴 2. Relative Rationality Theory rejects this invariance at the value level. The paper introduces Emotional Regret Expected Value as a cash-equivalent mechanism for representing the regret, relief, rejoicing, or missed-opportunity value generated when each possible outcome of one lottery is compared with the possible outcomes of the alternative lottery. EREV is then incorporated into Emotional Adjusted Value, so that EAV(Aᵢ|B) = Aᵢ + EREV(Aᵢ|B). The resulting emotionally adjusted outcomes are evaluated through Emotional Adjusted Expected Utility, where utility is applied to Decision-EAW positions rather than to raw monetary payoffs alone. The analysis shows that zero payoffs in the Allais Paradox need not be emotionally identical. The prospect of receiving zero in a lottery when the alternative guarantees €1 million may carry a different counterfactual emotional value from the prospect of receiving zero when both available lotteries already contain a high probability of receiving nothing. Consequently, EAV(0_B₁), EAV(0_A₂), and EAV(0_B₂) need not be equal. Within the RRT representation, the standard decomposition no longer applies because the terms being cancelled need not represent the same emotional-value objects. The paper concludes that the Allais pattern need not represent irrationality, but may reflect coherent emotional-adjusted evaluation under risk.

detail.abstract:
An Islamic financial institution operates under two binding authorities. A financial supervisor determines what it may do in law. A Sharia Supervisory Board determines what it may do in conscience, and in most such institutions the board's determinations are binding rather than advisory. Both authorities predate artificial intelligence, and neither has specified how its authority reaches an AI system.

The institution therefore does what institutions do when a new object arrives without a rule for it. It builds a second process. The AI system passes the civil governance machinery, and then, separately and usually later, it passes a Sharia review conducted by different people, on different evidence, producing different records. Two processes, two record sets, two answers to the question of whether the system may operate, and no defined behaviour when they disagree.

This specification proposes that the second process is unnecessary and that building it is the error. Its central move is structural: the Sharia Supervisory Board is constituted as an authority source at the Regulatory Floor of the MESA Framework [1], alongside the financial supervisor, so that its determinations cascade downward through the same governance machinery as civil regulation rather than running beside it. An institution operating this framework has one governance system with two authority sources at its floor.

Beneath that constitution sit a Maqasid risk frame, which classifies what an AI decision may harm in the terms the authority itself uses rather than in the terms of a Western risk taxonomy, and three threads into the institution's existing operational machinery: dual validation into model risk management, where a civil track and a Sharia track must both close before approval; the Halal data certification chain into data governance; and Sharia screening into vendor risk. Escalation is concurrent rather than sequential: a Sharia-material incident routes to the board alongside civil escalation, not after it.

The specification is unusually explicit about what it is not. No Sharia Supervisory Board has reviewed or endorsed it. The Halal data certification chain is author methodology that no standard-setter recognizes. No standard-setter has issued an instrument governing the interaction between Sharia governance and artificial intelligence. Academic proposals exist; a recognized standard does not. That is what makes this a proposal worth submitting rather than a restatement of practice, and equally what makes it unendorsed. Section 9 states each plainly and states what would falsify the framework.

It is a specification, not a certification scheme, and no conformity assessment body operates against it.

detail.abstract: The 2022 U.S. yield-curve inversion was the deepest in more than four decades, yet the recession many expected had not occurred by January 2025. We examine whether credit and equity conditions help explain why a recession did not follow. During the inversion, credit stress remained low and equity valuations stayed far from their financial-crisis levels. We use a structural Bayesian vector autoregression with traditional and narrative sign restrictions to distinguish policy-expectations shocks from financial-stress shocks. We find a persistent decline in industrial production after a financial-stress shock, but no clear evidence of a persistent decline after a policy-expectations shock or a term-spread shock identified separately from the policy rate. Finally, we construct conditional forecasts in which we hold the observed 2022-2024 paths of the federal funds rate and term spread fixed and replace the credit and equity paths with those from 2008-2010. After three years, forecast industrial production is about 18 percent lower under the crisis paths than under the observed paths. These findings suggest that forecasters should assess credit and equity conditions alongside the yield curve when evaluating recession risk.

detail.abstract: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) has played an essential role in Africa's digital transformation, particularly through digital identification, digital payments, data interchange, and digital government platforms. While DPI has the potential to increase access to public services, boost financial inclusion, and stimulate innovation, it may also result in new kinds of technological, institutional, and economic dependence in which vital infrastructure, expertise, financing, or data systems remain externally controlled. This essay investigates this tension using a qualitative comparative examination of Kenya, Rwanda, Nigeria, and Zambia. The study evaluates DPI across five dimensions, based on academic literature, policy papers, and institutional reports: inclusivity, interoperability, governance, local technological capacity, and digital sovereignty. The findings show that DPI can significantly increase service delivery and inclusivity, but its advantages are influenced by the governance arrangements surrounding infrastructure. The incidents also show that national control of digital systems does not necessarily imply technological autonomy. According to the report, Africa's DPI strategy should combine digital inclusion with improved local capabilities, open standards, transparent procurement, data protection, supplier diversification, and regional interoperability. The goal should not be technological isolation, but rather the ability of African institutions to engage meaningfully in the design, governance, and long-term development of the digital infrastructures on which their societies increasingly rely.

title: The Dual Currency Framework: A Market Mechanism for Public Goods

detail.abstract: This paper specifies the Dual Currency Framework, a market mechanism for diffuse effects at unbounded scale: the provision of public goods and the restraint of public harms. Every dollar of factor income mints a second dollar of public currency. It is directed at persons and the entities they own, funding those whose work an agent values and billing those whose harms they bear, through an allocation rule that pays a target more than in proportion to the money converged on it. The share of income moving through the public market is the income-weighted median of what participants declare, and a levy on income closes the books. The mechanism takes none of the canonical trilemma's corners: budget balance holds by construction, truthful declaration of the public market's preferred size is a dominant strategy, truthful placement is a best response to the field at the price-taking limit, and efficiency is aimed at and not claimed. It discovers what to fund and restrain, nothing being listed in advance, and holds at open scale, admitting anyone and verifying nobody. What restoration at that scale requires puts the first best out of reach; the paper states each cost by what it distorts and in which direction, determining no magnitude. Two kinds of measurement remain. Implementation waits on the rule's exponent, whether the field comes to rest and when the price-taking limit takes hold; the proposal waits on how near the mechanism comes to allocative efficiency over diffuse effects, against the methods of government in use.

detail.abstract: Mean willingness to pay from dichotomous-choice contingent valuation can depend on choices made after data collection. Using a survey of freshwater ecosystem protection in Southwest Florida, we compare nonparametric welfare rules, cutoff-slope conventions, and certainty calibration. Defensible specifications yield $69-$184 per household annually. Bootstrap results show that sampling stability depends on the specification: anchored tail rules are relatively stable, while some unanchored rules are highly unstable. We show that extrapolation sensitivity is governed by acceptance at the highest bid and that calibration also changes observed-support welfare. We recommend transparent sensitivity reporting and bid ladders that drive top-bid acceptance toward zero.

detail.abstract: In the United States, households often delay payments on unsecured debt for extended periods. These delinquencies are costly and can be a useful indicator of financial distress. Mortgage forbearance, a form of payment delay, saw swift but fleeting take-up early in the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite generous terms, most borrowers exited quickly. This paper reconciles these seemingly contradictory payment postponement patterns using a life-cycle model of mortgages and unsecured debt. Combining survey evidence with credit history data, our model resolves these facts through selection and expected income losses. Mortgage forbearance primarily attracted financially healthier homeowners, while anticipated income losses failed to materialize.

detail.abstract: Connected vehicles use situational awareness as these three sources mainly to build grounded on broadcast state messages, onboard sensors and infrastructure observations. These are good sources but create a consequential gap: an authenticated asserting identity can be done by a signed message but does not tell us that the asserting identity is where it claims to be. In this paper, a secure collaborative situational-awareness is established, wherein the ultra-wideband (UWB) time-of-flight ranging is seen as a proximity evidence channel and not as a channel of truth on its own. The framework secures short-lived pseudonymous vehicle credentials to authenticated UWB ranging transcripts, range-checks range, range rate, map geometry, and calibrates kinematic state, converts the resulting consistency evidence into a risk score. Some of the threats include replay, relay, Sybil behavior, distance reduction, non-line-of-sight bias, jamming, compromised insiders, and privacy leakage, which are all covered in a threat model. We define protocol state, fusion equation, trust update, failure modes that are safe and interfaces that are deployment-safe to cellular/direct V2X. A consistent simulation algorithm is provided to test the ranging performance, discrimination of attacks, cooperative riskestimation and latency-sensitivities. Synthetic experiments are provided to illustrate how the analytical design would behave with an ideal set of measurements: cooperative fusion reduces nominal ranging error, joint cryptographic-and-physical validity measures enhances attack separability, and time-to-collision-aware scoring suggests prioritizing the closeout of trajectories. The contribution is a systems framework that distinguishes the identity assurance, proximity assurance and safety risk and bridging them by making explicit uncertainty management. Implementation priorities and an experimental validation plan of closed-track studies and public-road studies both are the final aspects of the paper.

title: The Design Space of Market Provision for Public Goods

detail.abstract:
Incidence is the degree to which a good's effects fall on the agent who controls it. Where it is exclusive, purchase is itself the expression of valuation, and the pricing system allocates efficiently at any scale. Where it is diffuse, those the effects reach hold no lever over them: acting costs an agent the whole and returns a fraction, so what is held in common is underprovided and what is borne in common under-restrained, and both worsen as the population reached grows. 

Two responses are available-compute what the affected agents would have chosen and impose it, or restore the lever they would themselves have pulled. This paper takes the second and asks what fidelity to a restored lever requires. It finds compulsion necessary, a voluntary mechanism being subject to the failure it exists to remedy. It considers how the democratic vote reveals public values, by returning more to an agent's expression the more others hold it-the signature by which a diffusely incident effect is known. While both prove necessary, merging them with the private market's own principles raises multiple contradictions. This paper derives their costs, as prices of the response rather than of any design.

detail.abstract: Tabular machine learning systems are increasingly deployed in environments where the statistical properties of data change across time and geographic locations. Yet many development pipelines continue to evaluate models using random train-test splits that implicitly assume independent and identically distributed observations. Such evaluations can substantially overestimate deployment performance when nearby observations share contextual information or when future populations differ from historical training data. This paper examines how tabular machine learning models can be made more reliable under simultaneous temporal and geographic distribution shifts. Drawing on research on covariate shift, domain generalization, distributionally robust optimization, temporal validation, and modern tabular learning, the paper develops a shift-aware generalization framework that combines temporally ordered evaluation, geographic holdouts, domain-balanced training, invariant feature selection, distribution-aware reweighting, and continuous post-deployment monitoring. The analysis argues that model architecture alone is unlikely to solve distribution-shift problems. Instead, generalization depends on aligning the data-generating assumptions, validation design, feature engineering, training objective, and monitoring strategy with the environments in which predictions will ultimately be used. Evidence from benchmarks such as WILDS, Wild-Time, Folktables, and clinical prediction studies indicates that conventional in-distribution performance can conceal meaningful degradation under temporal or geographic shift. The paper therefore proposes a practical evaluation hierarchy in which temporal and spatial robustness are treated as first-class performance objectives rather than secondary robustness checks.

detail.abstract: This paper uncovers a new decomposition of asset returns that separates continuous price movements from jumps and resolves the well-known second-order confounding of drift and leverage, enabling separate inference on all four components. It reveals a unified mechanism behind two striking patterns in asset prices. First, the continuous component carries the overnight return into the trading day, while the jump component reverses part of this effect, generating offsetting momentum and reversal that largely cancel in the aggregate return. Second, persistent price movements during crises and boom periods are partially offset by sudden discontinuous adjustments. Together, these findings suggest a simple mechanism of price formation: continuous movements propagate price trends, while jumps counteract them.

detail.abstract: The rising concentration of major market indices has increasingly undermined the diversification benefits and increased the market risk of index investing. To address this issue, we propose a portfolio strategy designed to minimize variance relative to a given index fund. We decompose each stock's return into an index return and an idiosyncratic return, defined as the excess return over the index. By exploiting the resulting covariance structure-either between the index return and idiosyncratic returns or among the idiosyncratic returns themselves-we construct portfolios that enhance index efficiency by reducing portfolio variance. Using U.S. monthly stock data, we show that incorporating idiosyncratic returns into portfolio construction through this covariance structure consistently reduces out-of-sample variance relative to multiple basis index portfolios, including the S&P 500 index, the Equal-weighted S&P 500 index, and the CRSP value-weighted market portfolio. Crucially, portfolio returns remain comparable to those of the basis portfolios, leading to overall improvements in Sharpe ratios. These findings demonstrate that effective variance reduction can be achieved without sacrificing return performance.

detail.abstract: Human urine-derived fertilisers (HUDF) can recover nutrients for agricultural production, lowering emissions and supporting preparedness. However, insights on consumer responses to foods produced with these norm-laden inputs further up the supply chain and the necessary communication strategies to overcome potential negative emotions are scarce. In an online between-subjects experiment with Swedish consumers of plant-based milk alternatives, we examine the effect of a) disclosing fertiliser origin and b) two information framings: environmental and local-supply benefits, as well as historical/contextual normalisation. We study the implications for the willingness to pay (WTP) elicited under a potential product-delivery scenario, as well as for the perceptions of an oat drink produced with HUDF in terms of environmental friendliness, disgust, unfamiliarity and scariness. We find that benefit framing increased WTP and perceived environmental friendliness relative to basic disclosure. Normalising information reduced all three negative affective perceptions without a statistically detected increase in WTP. The findings support communicating the benefits of circular nutrient recovery while addressing negative emotional associations.

detail.abstract:
The Price of Verification reports that the fitness budget Θ*-the share of progenitor-dyad income committed jointly to raising children and to purchasing the old-age and health provision that allows a parent to survive to observe the outcome-is more stable across societies than either of its components. This supplement documents how far that test can be extended, which specification of the two cost ratios is correct and why it matters, and what the result does under alternative specifications and hostile robustness checks.
Extension is limited by one variable. No harmonised cross-national dataset of child-rearing cost exists, and the obvious substitute is unusable: the OECD’s net childcare cost indicator ranks Korea among the cheapest countries in the OECD in which to have small children, while total-cost estimates rank it the most expensive in the world. Both are correct. The divergence is itself evidence that the relevant cost parameter measures adolescent competitive expenditure rather than early-years care, which explains why childcare centred pronatalism has failed.
Specification is not a matter of convenience. Expressing the two ratios against GDP per capita rather than progenitor-dyad income, and assigning the child-directed family branch of social expenditure to fitness-access cost rather than netting it out of child-rearing cost, both depart from the model’s own definitions — and both destroy the result. Under those departures the coefficient of variation of Θ* is 17.9 per cent with a permutation p of 0.111, indistinguishable from chance. Under the specification the model actually calls for, it is 10.2 to 10.3 per cent with permutation p between 0.0005 and 0.004, and an estimated value of approximately 0.94 of dyad disposable income. That the answer is insensitive to whether the sample is eight, nine or ten countries is the substantive finding; under the misspecified version it is not. 
One country is excluded on data grounds. Singapore’s published cost figure derives from a personal-finance estimate containing no housing component, while the Chinese and American figures it would be compared against include one. Reconstructing the missing component moves Singapore across the sample mean rather than to either side of it, so it is uninformative in either direction.
Two hazards are tested. Measured child-rearing and fitness-access costs correlate at −0.83, raising the possibility that the invariance is manufactured by tax-financed in-kind provision suppressing one term while the taxation funding it inflates the other; isolating the child-directed component shows the relationship comes from pensions and health rather than from the contaminated channel. And an inequality correction to the income denominator, applied as an input adjustment rather than a predicted output, improves the fit at an implied cost elasticity above unity but does not survive a placebo test. 
A data specification is given for the thirty-to-forty country panel that would test the claim at conventional power rather than suggestively at n = 9.

detail.abstract: Financial markets may not be equally efficient across countries or economic conditions. This paper tests weak-form market efficiency across global equity markets, U.S. market sectors, and several market regimes, including the COVID-19 shock, post-COVID recovery, inflation and interest-rate shock, and recent AI-driven period. Market efficiency is evaluated using three statistical methods: the variance-ratio test, autocorrelation test, and runs test. The results show that most markets were generally consistent with weak-form efficiency during normal periods, while deviations became more common during major disruptions, particularly the COVID-19 shock. Emerging and frontier markets also showed greater evidence of serial dependence than developed markets. Mean-reversion and trend-following strategies were then compared with a buy-and-hold benchmark to determine whether these inefficiencies could be used in practice. However, the strategies did not consistently outperform the buy-and-hold benchmark. Overall, the changing levels of efficiency across markets and time periods support the Adaptive Market Hypothesis, which suggests that market efficiency changes as conditions and investor behavior evolve.

title: A Leakage-Safe Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Target Binding Prediction in DNA-Encoded Chemical Libraries

detail.title: A Leakage-Safe Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Target Binding Prediction in DNA-Encoded Chemical Libraries
detail.abstract: Early stage drug discovery increasingly relies on computational models to identify molecules that bind therapeutic protein targets because large scale experimental screening is costly and time intensive. Although recent representation learning methods have improved molecular prediction, many studies still rely on a single chemical view or evaluate models under settings that may overestimate generalization. Motivated by this gap, this study proposes BELKA-BERT, a leakage-aware information fusion framework for multilabel binding prediction that integrates three complementary molecular representations: ChemBERTa-based SMILES embeddings, Morgan fingerprint descriptors, and learnable embeddings of three synthesis building blocks. The framework was developed on a curated subset of the Leash BELKA dataset for binding prediction against BRD4, HSA, and sEH. To support realistic evaluation, label combination stratification was combined with building block triplet grouping to prevent synthesis recipe overlap between training and test partitions. The learning pipeline further combines domain-adaptive masked language modelling, supervised multimodal fusion, class imbalance correction, promiscuity regularisation, temperature scaling, and target-specific threshold optimisation to improve ranking performance and decision reliability. On the leakage-aware working subset, the final fusion model achieved a micro average precision of 0.9722; Multi-seed evaluation on the class-realistic 3M-molecule BELKA working corpus, three-seed evaluation yielded micro-AP of 0.7917±0.0033, which is the more representative estimate of prospective screening performance. Controlled ablation experiments show that fingerprint removal causes the largest performance drop, confirming that explicit substructural information provides strong complementary value beyond transformer sequence embeddings. These results support BELKA-BERT as a robust, interpretable, and reproducible framework for trustworthy multi-target virtual screening.

detail.abstract: State-dependent local projections (LPs) are widely used to study how causal effects vary as a function of economic states, but shock exogeneity alone does not identify this response function. We show that identification follows when the underlying conditional mean is linear in the shock with a state-dependent coefficient, a condition satisfied in canonical micro-macro environments, including first-order perturbation solutions of heterogeneous-agent and macro-finance models. Even then, standard linear-interaction LPs generally recover only a projection of the response function, motivating LPs with nonparametric state dependence. We develop a sieve estimator and establish pointwise and uniform inference for micro-macro panels, where a distinctive challenge is that the estimator can converge at different rates across the state space. Applied to firm investment, the method uncovers a hump-shaped response to monetary policy shocks and shows that standard linear-interaction LPs substantially understate the aggregate role of financial heterogeneity.

title: The Stories We Tell: Societal Narratives and Support for the Far Right
affiliations: University of Zurich - Department Finance, WZB Berlin Social Science Center,  and Technische Universität Berlin (TU Berlin)

detail.title: The Stories We Tell: Societal Narratives and Support for the Far Right

publicationDetails.detailsText: NHH Dept. of Economics Discussion Paper No. 14/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: Norwegian School of Economics, Department of Economics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: In two studies using AI-assisted qualitative interviews, we ask a representative sample of the German electorate (N = 1, 013) to reflect on the most important societal events of the last 15 years. We document that far-right supporters construct systematically different narratives about the recent past. First, they recall different events-with a strong focus on migration-related issues. Second, even when they do consider the same events, they are more likely to blame the establishment and describe events more negatively and with greater emotional intensity. We further document that these narratives are associated with policy preferences, and that farright supporters are more inclined than supporters of other parties to prioritize cultural over economic issues. Together, our findings reveal that partisan divides extend to how citizens remember and interpret shared national experiences.

title: Bad Markets, Bad Advisors? Investor Scrutiny and Recorded Financial Advisor Misconduct
affiliations: Georgetown University - McDonough School of Business,  and

detail.title: Bad Markets, Bad Advisors? Investor Scrutiny and Recorded Financial Advisor Misconduct

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: No outside funding.

detail.abstract: Recorded financial advisor misconduct rises sharply when stock market performance is poor. We ask whether this reflects more wrongdoing, investors recasting losses as misconduct, or greater detection of existing misconduct. The evidence is most consistent with detection. Geographic exposure to corporate fraud and the Madoff scandal-trust shocks unrelated to the performance underlying the complaints we study-also increase recorded misconduct. Poor returns also increase directly verifiable violations, such as unauthorized trading, and complaints that yield no adverse finding or payment. Effects are strongest among advisors with high ex-ante misconduct risk. Recorded misconduct thus reflects both wrongdoing and investor scrutiny.

title: Organizational Denizenship - Membership, Liminality and the Worker Who Is Present but Not Enrolled

detail.title: Organizational Denizenship - Membership, Liminality and the Worker Who Is Present but Not Enrolled

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is an advocate and an in-house legal and compliance practitioner. That professional position informed the author's interest in the subject matter of this article and is disclosed accordingly. The author is also a member of a class of employees that benefits from arrangements of the kind this article examines, including eligibility for discretionary distributions from which outsourced workers on the same premises are excluded. This is disclosed not because it gives the author an interest in the conclusions reached — it does not, and those conclusions are adverse to that position — but because a reader is entitled to know from where the argument is written. The case discussed in this article is a composite, constructed for analytical purposes from arrangements that recur widely in outsourced service provision. It is not a report of events at any identified organisation. No confidential or privileged information has been used, no institution, employer or client is identified, and the article relies exclusively on published sources. The author has no financial interest in the arguments advanced and received no consideration, funding or benefit in connection with this work. The views expressed are the author's own and are not advanced on behalf of any employer or client. This article is one of three studies of a single arrangement. The same declaration applies to each.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. These are doctrinal and theoretical articles involving no human participants, no clinical data and no personal data, and relying exclusively on published legal and scholarly sources.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
A watchman stands at the gate of an organisation for nine years. He wears a uniform, holds its keys, knows which vehicles belong and which faces are wrong, and is invited to its annual staff event. He is not on its payroll, and on that single ground the organisation's disciplinary code, grievance machinery, welfare fund, bonus scheme, bereavement process and duty of fairness do not apply to him. This article asks what his status is.

It argues that the answer is not adequately given by any of the categories presently available. It is not exclusion, because he is included for every purpose that costs the organisation nothing. It is not employment, because the obligations have been contracted elsewhere. It is not caste, because caste at least assigns a place. And it is not statelessness, because he holds, formally, two memberships rather than none.

The article proposes that it is a distinct condition with four properties. Membership is conferred and withdrawn by the same party according to what recognition costs it, so that the status is selective, unilateral and asymmetric. The two formal memberships he holds operate not as redundancy but as each other's excuse, producing a negative conflict of jurisdiction. His position combines the immobility of caste with the illegibility of statelessness, which are properties that do not ordinarily co-occur. And the resulting indeterminacy is not a failure to classify but a classification whose content is the absence of obligation, maintained because it is useful.

It further argues that the exclusion itself is not new — employers have always sought labour without the status that attaches to obtaining it — but that the interposition of a second employer defeats the doctrines built to catch earlier attempts, because those doctrines correct a misdescription and this arrangement contains none. Where courts have nonetheless reached the principal, they have done so by a route operating as a sword rather than a shield: available only to those able to litigate, which this population is not. The article further argues that multi-factor tests are structurally unsuited to the problem, since a published test functions as a drafting brief, and that the criteria which survive avoidance are those attaching to presence rather than to status — presence being the one fact an organisation cannot restructure without surrendering what it purchased.

Drawing on Arendt's analysis of statelessness and the right to have rights, on the anthropology of liminality from Van Gennep through Turner to Szakolczai's concept of permanent liminality, and on Hammar's and Standing's work on denizenship, the article names the condition organisational denizenship and sets out its markers — including a taxonomy of uniform regimes which, it argues, encode jurisdictional rather than operational distinctions. It argues that the condition is not relieved by the route Arendt identified as the last one available, since the protections the criminal law confers are themselves distributed by capacity, and that this class in any event operates under a social presumption that the legal one cannot displace. It closes by asking what would confer standing, and argues that the answer is not better treatment but enrolment of a different kind.

title: The Gig Economy and the Precariat: Rethinking the Definition Of "Employee" Under Nigerian Labour Law

detail.title: The Gig Economy and the Precariat: Rethinking the Definition Of "Employee" Under Nigerian Labour Law

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded.

detail.abstract: The rise of digitally-mediated, platform-based work has unsettled the conceptual foundations of labour law across the world, and Nigeria is no exception. Ride-hailing and delivery platforms such as Uber, Bolt, and Gokada, together with online freelancing platforms, have drawn hundreds of thousands of Nigerians into arrangements that bear the hallmarks of employment, direction, control, economic dependence, while being contractually labelled as "partnerships" or independent contracting. This article examines whether the statutory definition of "worker" under section 91 of the Labour Act, Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, and the judicially developed tests for distinguishing a contract of service from a contract for service, remain adequate to protect gig workers from precarity. Drawing on the sole reported Nigerian adjudication on the point, Oladapo Olatunji & Anor v Uber Technologies System Nigeria Limited & 2 Ors, and on comparative developments in the United Kingdom, South Africa, Ghana, Canada, and the European Union, the article argues that Nigeria's binary employee/independent-contractor classification is structurally incapable of capturing the intermediate reality of platform work. It situates the Nigerian gig worker within Guy Standing's theory of the precariat, and contends that without legislative or judicial intervention, an increasing share of Nigeria's already largely informal workforce will remain outside the protective reach of labour, pension, and compensation legislation. The article concludes with recommendations for a statutorily defined intermediate category of "dependent contractor," a rebuttable presumption of employment triggered by platform control, and extension of social security schemes to platform-mediated work.

title: A Global Stress Regime-Switching Framework for Multi-Country Mortality Risk Modeling
affiliations: Western University, Canada, Oregon State University and Western University

detail.title: A Global Stress Regime-Switching Framework for Multi-Country Mortality Risk Modeling
detail.abstract: We develop a global stress regime-switching framework for modeling aggregate mortality risk across multiple countries under systemic stress, motivated by mortality-linked securities. The model operates directly on aggregate mortality indices constructed from death counts and exposures, avoiding the need for age-disaggregated data or high-dimensional joint latent structures. Country-level dynamics are first estimated independently using hidden Markov models with sign-identified truncated-Gaussian emissions representing Regular, Shock, and Recovery regimes.Cross-country dependence is introduced through a product-based systemic proxy constructed from posterior Shock probabilities. This proxy is used to calibrate a latent two-state global process governing the timing of joint mortality deterioration. Country transition matrices are modified under Calm and Stress regimes subject to a marginal-preservation condition that keeps long-run Shock occupancies unchanged. The framework also separates occurrence dependence, driven by the global state process, from magnitude dependence, represented through residual correlation in Regular periods and a Gumbel copula during joint Stress-period Shock events.The model is applied to the United States and Canada over 1933–2022 and to Austria, Belgium, and the Netherlands over 1947–2022. Relative to benchmark models, including a multivariate jump-diffusion specification, it improves in-sample fit and out-of-sample predictive accuracy. Bootstrap results indicate that these gains are attributable to the modeled cross-country dependence structure.

title: Fragmentation or Specialization? Economic Sorting in the Public Blockchain Ecosystem
affiliations: Seoul National University, Seoul National University - College of Business Administration and Hansung University

detail.title: Fragmentation or Specialization? Economic Sorting in the Public Blockchain Ecosystem

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N.A.
declarations.funderStatement: Jungsuk Han and Jongsub Lee gratefully acknowledge financial support from the Institute of Management Research at Seoul National University.

detail.abstract: The proliferation of public blockchain rails need not fragment monetary networks; it can instead reflect economic specialization. We develop a model in which heterogeneous economic functions sort across validation rails according to their security intensity. A single-crossing condition assigns high-value, security-sensitive activity to high-validation rails and frequent, low-value activity to lower-cost rails. We then embed this sorting mechanism in a supermodular adoption game. Because network effects operate across distinct functions of the same monetary claim, adoption in one function complements adoption in others even when those functions reside on different rails. The strength of these cross-function complementarities depends on interoperability, giving rise to low-and high-adoption equilibria and rendering the high-adoption equilibrium fragile to disruptions in interoperability or par convertibility. Using transaction-level data for USDC and USDT across seven major blockchains, we find that more secure rails process larger transfers, and issuer-level growth traces the model's high-and low adoption branches. An early-2024 Ethereum fee shock further shifts activity away from small transfers and toward larger transactions. Together, our results suggest that multi-chain stablecoin activity can preserve monetary network effects through interoperable specialization rather than uniformity on a single ledger.

title: The Sword and The Seal: Crypto Asset Recovery as Quasi-Legal Mobilization Under Fragmented Authority
affiliations: and Wuhan University

detail.title: The Sword and The Seal: Crypto Asset Recovery as Quasi-Legal Mobilization Under Fragmented Authority

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No
declarations.funderStatement: No

detail.abstract: How are digital property rights protected when crypto assets move rapidly across borderless infrastructures, and when information and remedial capacity are fragmented across multiple public and private domains? To unpack this problem, this article develops a four-task model of quasi-legal mobilization under fragmented authority. We use recovery after crypto hacks as our primary case study. Drawing on 128 interviews, 4,775 public documents, and a dataset of 468 major crypto hacks from 2016 to 2026, we show how legal intermediaries characterize the wrong, substantiate claims with portable proof, authorize relief, and sequence forums. These practices offer an emerging institutional template for protecting property rights in the digital context. However, it may also make relief dependent on victims' access to institutional leverage and elite intermediaries. The article recasts legal intermediaries as central institutional actors and shows how secondorder legal consciousness enables legality to travel across fragmented authority.

title: Detecting Financial Risk Before Loss: A Two-Stage Controllership Method for Supply Chain and Retail Operations

detail.title: Detecting Financial Risk Before Loss: A Two-Stage Controllership Method for Supply Chain and Retail Operations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that this research was conducted in the absence of any commercial, financial, or personal relationships that could be construed or perceived as a potential conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant, financial support, or funding from any agency, corporation, or public, commercial, or not-for-profit sector. The study was entirely self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: Financial controllership operates as a lagging function. It identifies compliance variances and transaction errors after decisions are final and losses are absorbed, producing a record of what happened rather than a control that could have changed it. This paper presents a two-stage method that moves detection to the point of decision. Stage One scores where financial risk concentrates in a set of business processes and assigns a dollar value to controlling each one, using a deterministic model with auditable equations across four categories of protection. The result is a ranked, dollar-valued map of where controls are worth building. Stage Two builds control at each priority point. What matters most is where it sits. A control must run inside the approval path, while commitment can still be stopped. Once a price, an agreement, or a funding term is booked, it governs every transaction that follows, and no later review can undo what it has already set in motion. The paper examines four points where these commitments concentrate. They are vendor and transaction approval, agreement execution, internal financial reporting, and high velocity peak events, and the paper specifies the control built at each. Because these controls are increasingly built on artificial intelligence, a second problem arises. The method applies controllership to artificial intelligence itself. Language classification and financial calculation run in separate channels, a second process re-derives the result from source data, and any disagreement locks the transaction for human review, so the automation cannot become a new source of error or loss. The method is industry-agnostic, implemented and validated in large-scale retail and supply chain operations. It can be applied to any organization regardless of size, type and nature.
